name: Squash-and-stretch bounce

source.description: Two inspected references drop objects (a ball, ice cubes) with physical bounce timing and squash on contact.

technique: Objects fall with gravity-like acceleration, stretch while fast, squash on contact and rebound lower and quicker each time, which gives flat graphics weight and material.
purpose: Physicality and charm for entrances of objects, icons and letters.
visual_behaviour: Drop, squash, smaller rebound, smaller squash, settle; about 0.8-1.4 s in total.
mechanics: power2.in falls and power2.out rises; rebound height x decay and duration x sqrt(decay); 50 ms squash, 100 ms recovery; scale about the base.

decomposition.timing: First fall about 0.4-0.45 s; each rebound about 60% shorter in time.

failure_modes: Squash on rigid objects (glass, metal) looks wrong; set squash to 0
Bouncing everything makes the piece toy-like

provenance.observed: A ball bounces with visible squash on contact, labelled with an annotation.
Ice cubes drop into a glass and settle with small bounces (approx., from overview spacing).

licensing_notes: Technique only (a classic animation principle), observed in user-supplied references.
